reasoning_content:
App is up. CMS is up. Memory is down to 459MB. Now, the boards build needs about 1.8GB. There's only 459MB of free space, but the boards build has been cached. However, it may still get OOM-killed. Let's try it with careful monitoring. If boards gets OOM-killed, we might be able to free up a bit of memory... Actually, if we stop the app temporarily, we can secure about 1.9GB for the boards build, and then restart the app afterwards (the app build has also been cached).

Strategy: Stop the app (free up about 1.9GB) → start boards (about 1.8GB, fits) → restart the app (about 1.9GB) → check whether all three coexist (1.9+1.8+1.8+2.3 for containers = 7.8 > 7.6, slightly over, but esbuild's child process usage is smaller, so it might just barely fit).

Actually, let's try starting boards directly first — the cached build is lighter (compilation can be skipped, only watch mode). If it gets killed, fall back to the swap-out method.

action.command:
cd /workspace
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
# Free memory: stop app temporarily so boards build has room
kill -TERM -- -201563 2>/dev/null; sleep 8
ps aux | grep -E "run-executor|nx.js" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill 2>/dev/null; sleep 4
free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
setsid nohup bash -c 'exec just serve --apps=boards < /dev/zero' > /tmp/fin-boards.log 2>&1 &
echo "boards pid $!"
for i in $(seq 1 9); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:39003/ 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "boards UP check $i"; break; }
  echo "check $i: boards=$code avail=$(free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print $6}')MB"
  sleep 40
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "boards: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:39003/ 2>/dev/null; free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
